Variant Library

Halma is an abstract strategy race game invented in 1883 by George Howard Monks, an American surgeon in Boston. Played on a 16×16 checkered board, each player occupies a triangular corner camp and races all their pieces to the diagonally opposite camp. Pieces may step to any adjacent square or chain-hop over any adjacent piece without capturing.

This library includes 2 playable variants.

  • Standard 2-Player — 19 pieces per player on a 16×16 board, two opposing corner camps
  • Standard 4-Player — 13 pieces per player, one camp in each of the four corners
